Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: OCT signal
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: Complex phasor representation of the OCT signal
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
OCT signals $S_{OCT}$ can be described by complex phasors of the form

$$
S _ {O C T} (\mathbf {x}, t) = A (\mathbf {x}, t) \exp [ i \phi (\mathbf {x}, t) ] \tag {1}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Binormal (or Beckmann) distribution
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: Characterizes the complex noise signal in the complex plane
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
Hence, the complex noise signal is characterized by a binormal (or Beckmann) distribution $p_{ri}$ in the complex plane [22,23]:

$$
p _ {r i} (r _ {n o i s e}, i _ {n o i s e}) = \frac {1}{2 \pi \sigma^ {2}} \exp \left[ - \frac {r _ {n o i s e} ^ {2} + i _ {n o i s e} ^ {2}}{2 \sigma^ {2}} \right]. \tag {2}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Probability density function of the noise amplitude
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
The probability density function $p_A$ of the noise amplitude $A_{noise}$ is represented by the Rayleigh distribution (which can be derived by transforming Eq. (2) to polar coordinates and integrating over all angles $\phi$ ) [22]

$$
p _ {A} (A _ {\text { noise }}) = \frac {A _ {\text { noise }}}{\sigma^ {2}} \exp \left[ - \frac {A _ {\text { noise }} ^ {2}}{2 \sigma^ {2}} \right]. \tag {3}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Mean amplitude of a general PDF
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: The mean amplitude $\overline{u}$ and variance $\sigma_{U}^{2}$ of a general PDF $p_{U}(u)$ is given by $\overline{u} = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} up_{U}(u) du$ and $\sigma_{U}^{2} = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (u - \overline{u})^{2} p_{U}(u) du$ , respectively [22].

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Variance of a general PDF
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: The mean amplitude $\overline{u}$ and variance $\sigma_{U}^{2}$ of a general PDF $p_{U}(u)$ is given by $\overline{u} = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} up_{U}(u) du$ and $\sigma_{U}^{2} = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} (u - \overline{u})^{2} p_{U}(u) du$ , respectively [22].

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Mean amplitude of the noise
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
The mean amplitude $\overline{A_{noise}}$ and the variance $\sigma_{noise}^{2}$ of $p_{A}$ can be computed as

$$
\overline {{{A _ {n o i s e}}}} = \sqrt {\frac {\pi}{2}} \sigma , \tag {4}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Variance of the noise amplitude
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
The mean amplitude $\overline{A_{noise}}$ and the variance $\sigma_{noise}^{2}$ of $p_{A}$ can be computed as

$$
\overline {{{A _ {n o i s e}}}} = \sqrt {\frac {\pi}{2}} \sigma , \tag {4},
$$

$$
\sigma_ {n o i s e} ^ {2} = \left(2 - \frac {\pi}{2}\right) \sigma^ {2}. \tag {5}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: PDF of the measured amplitudes incorporating both signal and noise (Rice distribution)
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
the PDF of the measured amplitudes incorporating both signal and noise is represented by a Rice distribution

$$
p _ {A} (A, A _ {\text { noise }}) = \frac {A _ {\text { noise }}}{\sigma^ {2}} \exp \left[ - \frac {A _ {\text { noise }} ^ {2} + A ^ {2}}{2 \sigma^ {2}} \right] B _ {0} \left[ \frac {A _ {\text { noise }} A}{\sigma^ {2}} \right]. \tag {6}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Mean amplitude in an image pixel
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
The mean amplitude $\overline{A}$ and variance $\sigma_{A}^{2}$ in an image pixel are observed as

$$
\overline {{A}} = \sqrt {\frac {\pi}{2}} \sigma L _ {1 / 2} \left[ - \frac {A ^ {2}}{2 \sigma^ {2}} \right], \tag {7},
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Variance of the amplitude in an image pixel
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
The mean amplitude $\overline{A}$ and variance $\sigma_{A}^{2}$ in an image pixel are observed as

$$
\overline {{A}} = \sqrt {\frac {\pi}{2}} \sigma L _ {1 / 2} \left[ - \frac {A ^ {2}}{2 \sigma^ {2}} \right], \tag {7},
$$

$$
\sigma_ {A} ^ {2} = A ^ {2} + 2 \sigma^ {2} + \frac {\pi}{2} \sigma L _ {1 / 2} ^ {2} \left[ - \frac {A ^ {2}}{2 \sigma^ {2}} \right], \tag {8}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: PDF of the intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: transform of $A = \sqrt{I}$ is performed such that the PDFs are rendered into $p_{I}(I) = p_{A}(A = \sqrt{I}) \left| \frac{dA}{dI} \right|$ .

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: PDF for noise intensities
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
The resulting PDFs for noise ( $p_{I}(I_{noise})$ ) and signal intensities ( $p_{I}(I, I_{noise})$ ) are

$$
p _ {I} (I _ {\text { noise }}) = \frac {1}{2 \sigma^ {2}} \exp \left[ - \frac {I _ {\text { noise }}}{2 \sigma^ {2}} \right], \tag {9},
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Probability density function of signal intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $p _ {I} (I, I _ {\text { noise }}) = \frac {1}{2 \sigma^ {2}} \exp \left[ - \frac {I _ {\text { noise }} + I}{2 \sigma^ {2}} \right] B _ {0} \left[ \frac {\sqrt {I _ {\text { noise }} I}}{\sigma^ {2}} \right]$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ p _ {I} (I, I _ {\text { noise }}) = \frac {1}{2 \sigma^ {2}} \exp \left[ - \frac {I _ {\text { noise }} + I}{2 \sigma^ {2}} \right] B _ {0} \left[ \frac {\sqrt {I _ {\text { noise }} I}}{\sigma^ {2}} \right], \tag {10} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Mean noise intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \overline {{{I _ {\text { noise } e}}}} = 2 \sigma^ {2}, \tag {11} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Variance of noise intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \sigma_ {I _ {\text { noise }}} ^ {2} = 4 \sigma^ {4}, \tag {12} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Mean signal intensity
Variance of signal intensity
Magnitude averaged intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
Magnitude averaging uses the absolute values of N spatially and/or temporally separated signals (e.g., N pixels in a 2D or 3D kernel or N repeated measurements at the same spatial pixel location but at different time points):

$$
\langle I \rangle_ {M A G} = \frac {1}{N} \sum_ {j = 1} ^ {N} I _ {j}. \tag {15}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Mean of magnitude-averaged noise intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
Nevertheless, the mean intensity values and intensity variances can be calculated for Rayleigh distributed noise and Rician signals affected by

random noise, respectively, as

$$
\overline {{\langle I _ {\text { noise }} \rangle_ {M A G}}} = 2 \sigma^ {2} = \overline {{I _ {\text { noise }}}}, \tag {16}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Variance of magnitude-averaged noise intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
Nevertheless, the mean intensity values and intensity variances can be calculated for Rayleigh distributed noise and Rician signals affected by

random noise, respectively, as

$$
\langle \sigma_ {I _ {\text { noise }}} ^ {2} \rangle_ {M A G} = \frac {1}{N} 4 \sigma^ {4} = \frac {1}{N} \sigma_ {I _ {\text { noise }}} ^ {2}, \tag {17}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Variance of magnitude-averaged signal intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
Nevertheless, the mean intensity values and intensity variances can be calculated for Rayleigh distributed noise and Rician signals affected by

random noise, respectively, as

$$
\langle \sigma_ {I} ^ {2} \rangle_ {M A G} = \frac {1}{N} 4 \sigma^ {2} (I + \sigma^ {2}) = \frac {1}{N} \sigma_ {I} ^ {2}. \tag {19}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Mean of complex-averaged noise intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
This reduction of the noise amplitude variance translates into a reduction of both the mean noise intensity as well as of its variance:

$$
\overline {{\langle I _ {\text { noise }} \rangle_ {C P X}}} = \frac {1}{N} 2 \sigma^ {2} = \frac {1}{N} \overline {{I _ {\text { noise }}}}, \tag {20}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Signal-to-noise ratio for a single signal
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.scope_ref: Signal-to-noise performance without noise bias correction
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: we find the following SNRs for single signals, N magnitude averaged signals, and N complex averaged signals, respectively: $$ \mathrm{SNR} _ {1} = \frac {\bar {I}}{\sigma_ {I _ {\text { noise }}}} = \frac {I + \overline {{I _ {\text { noise }}}}}{\sigma_ {I _ {\text { noise }}}}, \tag {24} $$

method_ref.surface: Signal-to-noise performance without noise bias correction

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Signal-to-noise ratio for N magnitude averaged signals
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $\mathrm{SNR} _ {M A G} = \frac {\overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {M A G}}}}{\left\langle \sigma_ {I _ {\text { noise }}} \right\rangle_ {M A G}} = \frac {I + \overline {{I _ {\text { noise }}}}}{\frac {1}{\sqrt {N}} \sigma_ {I _ {\text { noise }}}} = \sqrt {N} \cdot \mathrm{SNR} _ {1}$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \mathrm{SNR} _ {M A G} = \frac {\overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {M A G}}}}{\left\langle \sigma_ {I _ {\text { noise }}} \right\rangle_ {M A G}} = \frac {I + \overline {{I _ {\text { noise }}}}}{\frac {1}{\sqrt {N}} \sigma_ {I _ {\text { noise }}}} = \sqrt {N} \cdot \mathrm{SNR} _ {1}, \tag {25} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Signal-to-noise ratio for N complex averaged signals
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $\mathrm{SNR} _ {C P X} = \frac {\overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {C P X}}}}{\left\langle \sigma_ {I _ {\text {noise}}} \right\rangle_ {C P X}} = \frac {I + \frac {1}{N} \overline {{I _ {\text {noise}}}}}{\frac {1}{N} \sigma_ {I _ {\text {noise}}}} = N \cdot \mathrm{SNR} _ {1} - (N - 1)$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \mathrm{SNR} _ {C P X} = \frac {\overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {C P X}}}}{\left\langle \sigma_ {I _ {\text {noise}}} \right\rangle_ {C P X}} = \frac {I + \frac {1}{N} \overline {{I _ {\text {noise}}}}}{\frac {1}{N} \sigma_ {I _ {\text {noise}}}} = N \cdot \mathrm{SNR} _ {1} - (N - 1). \tag {26} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Ratio of complex averaged SNR to magnitude averaged SNR
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ SNR_{CPX}/SNR_{MAG} = (N - (N - 1)/SNR_{1})/\sqrt{N} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Borderline input SNR for which magnitude and complex averaging perform equally well
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \mathrm{SNR} _ {1, \text { borderline }} = 1 + \frac {1}{\sqrt {N}} \tag {27} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Signal-to-noise ratio for a single signal with zero signal intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \mathrm{SNR} _ {1} (I = 0) = \frac {\overline {{I _ {\text { noise }}}}}{\sigma_ {I _ {\text { noise }}}} = 1, \tag {28} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Signal-to-noise ratio after magnitude averaging in the absence of a signal
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $\mathrm{SNR} _ {M A G} (I = 0) = \frac {\overline {{I _ {n o i s e}}}}{\frac {1}{\sqrt {N}} \sigma_ {I _ {n o i s e}}} = \sqrt {N}$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.scope_ref: SNR in absence of a signal (noise floor only)
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \mathrm{SNR} _ {M A G} (I = 0) = \frac {\overline {{I _ {n o i s e}}}}{\frac {1}{\sqrt {N}} \sigma_ {I _ {n o i s e}}} = \sqrt {N}, \tag {29} $$

method_ref.surface: SNR in absence of a signal (noise floor only)

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Signal-to-noise ratio after complex averaging in the absence of a signal
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $\mathrm{SNR} _ {C P X} (I = 0) = \frac {\frac {1}{N} \overline {{I _ {n o i s e}}}}{\frac {1}{N} \sigma_ {I _ {n o i s e}}} = 1$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.scope_ref: SNR in absence of a signal (noise floor only)
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \mathrm{SNR} _ {C P X} (I = 0) = \frac {\frac {1}{N} \overline {{I _ {n o i s e}}}}{\frac {1}{N} \sigma_ {I _ {n o i s e}}} = 1. \tag {30} $$

method_ref.surface: SNR in absence of a signal (noise floor only)

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Noise bias corrected average signal intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $\bar {I} ^ {\prime} = \bar {I} - \overline {{I _ {n o i s e}}} = I + 2 \sigma^ {2} - 2 \sigma^ {2} = I$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.scope_ref: SNR analysis with noise bias correction
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \bar {I} ^ {\prime} = \bar {I} - \overline {{I _ {n o i s e}}} = I + 2 \sigma^ {2} - 2 \sigma^ {2} = I, \tag {31} $$

method_ref.surface: SNR analysis with noise bias correction

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Noise bias corrected average magnitude signal intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $\overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {M A G}}} ^ {\prime} = \overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {M A G}}} - \overline {{\langle I _ {n o i s e} \rangle_ {M A G}}}$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {M A G}}} ^ {\prime} = \overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {M A G}}} - \overline {{\langle I _ {n o i s e} \rangle_ {M A G}}} = I + 2 \sigma^ {2} - 2 \sigma^ {2} = I, \tag {32} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Noise bias corrected average complex signal intensity
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $\overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {C P X}}} ^ {\prime} = \overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {C P X}}} - \overline {{\langle I _ {\text { noise }} \rangle_ {C P X}}}$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {C P X}}} ^ {\prime} = \overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {C P X}}} - \overline {{\langle I _ {\text { noise }} \rangle_ {C P X}}} = I + \frac {1}{N} 2 \sigma^ {2} - \frac {1}{N} 2 \sigma^ {2} = I. \tag {33} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Noise bias corrected SNR for single measurement
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ S N R _ {1} ^ {\prime} = \frac {\bar {I} ^ {\prime}}{\sigma_ {I _ {\text { noise }}}} = \frac {I}{2 \sigma^ {2}}, \tag {34} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Noise bias corrected SNR for magnitude averaging
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $S N R _ {M A G} ^ {\prime} = \frac {\overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {M A G}}} ^ {\prime}}{\left\langle \sigma_ {I _ {\text {noise}}} \right\rangle_ {M A G}} = \sqrt {N} \frac {I}{2 \sigma^ {2}} = \sqrt {N} \cdot S N R _ {1} ^ {\prime}$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ S N R _ {M A G} ^ {\prime} = \frac {\overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {M A G}}} ^ {\prime}}{\left\langle \sigma_ {I _ {\text {noise}}} \right\rangle_ {M A G}} = \sqrt {N} \frac {I}{2 \sigma^ {2}} = \sqrt {N} \cdot S N R _ {1} ^ {\prime}, \tag {35} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Noise bias corrected SNR for complex averaging
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $S N R _ {C P X} ^ {\prime} = \frac {\overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {C P X}}} ^ {\prime}}{\left\langle \sigma_ {I _ {\text {noise}}} \right\rangle_ {C P X}} = N \frac {I}{2 \sigma^ {2}} = N \cdot S N R _ {1} ^ {\prime}$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ S N R _ {C P X} ^ {\prime} = \frac {\overline {{\langle I \rangle_ {C P X}}} ^ {\prime}}{\left\langle \sigma_ {I _ {\text {noise}}} \right\rangle_ {C P X}} = N \frac {I}{2 \sigma^ {2}} = N \cdot S N R _ {1} ^ {\prime}. \tag {36} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Penalty factor for complex averaging of N signals
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.scope_ref: Complex signal averaging in case of axial motion
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
the resulting relative signal reduction corresponds to the penalty factor $P(N)$ :

$$
P (N) = \frac {1}{N} \left| \sum_ {j = 1} ^ {N} e ^ {i 2 \pi W _ {j}} \right| \tag {37}
$$

method_ref.surface: Complex signal averaging in case of axial motion

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Penalty factor when averaging N signals with relative separation W
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $P (N, W) = \frac {1}{N} \left| \sum_ {j = 1} ^ {N} e ^ {i 2 \pi W j} \right| = \frac {1}{N} \left| \frac {\sin [ \pi W (N + 1) ]}{\sin [ \pi W ]} e ^ {i \pi N W} - 1 \right|$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.scope_ref: Complex signal averaging in case of axial motion
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
The penalty factor $P(N)$ when averaging N signals with relative separation $W_{j} = W$ is

$$
P (N, W) = \frac {1}{N} \left| \sum_ {j = 1} ^ {N} e ^ {i 2 \pi W j} \right| = \frac {1}{N} \left| \frac {\sin [ \pi W (N + 1) ]}{\sin [ \pi W ]} e ^ {i \pi N W} - 1 \right|. \tag {38}
$$

method_ref.surface: Complex signal averaging in case of axial motion

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Bulk phase shift between the m-th A-line in a reference frame and the corresponding m-th A-scan in other frames
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $\Delta \phi_ {b u l k} ^ {(m)} = \arg \left[ \sum_ {z = z _ {0}} ^ {z _ {\max}} \left(A _ {m} ^ {j} (z) e ^ {i \phi_ {m} ^ {j} (z)}\right) \left(A _ {m} ^ {\text {ref}} (z) e ^ {i \phi_ {m} ^ {\text {ref}} (z)}\right) ^ {*} \right] = \arg \left[ \sum_ {z = z _ {0}} ^ {z _ {\max}} A _ {m} ^ {j} (z) A _ {m} ^ {r e f} (z) e ^ {i [ \phi_ {m} ^ {j} (z) - \phi_ {m} ^ {r e f} (z) ]} \right]$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
the bulk phase shift $\Delta\phi_{bulk}$ between the m-th A-line in a reference frame (ref) and the corresponding m-th A-scan in other frames to be averaged can be calculated by computing the angle of the weighted complex signal average along every A-scan:

$$
\begin{array}{l} \Delta \phi_ {b u l k} ^ {(m)} = \arg \left[ \sum_ {z = z _ {0}} ^ {z _ {\max}} \left(A _ {m} ^ {j} (z) e ^ {i \phi_ {m} ^ {j} (z)}\right) \left(A _ {m} ^ {\text {ref}} (z) e ^ {i \phi_ {m} ^ {\text {ref}} (z)}\right) ^ {*} \right] = \tag {39} \\ = \arg \left[ \sum_ {z = z _ {0}} ^ {z _ {\max}} A _ {m} ^ {j} (z) A _ {m} ^ {r e f} (z) e ^ {i [ \phi_ {m} ^ {j} (z) - \phi_ {m} ^ {r e f} (z) ]} \right] \\ \end{array}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.symbol: $S _ {O C T} ^ {(m o c o)} (x, z)$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Axial motion corrected (moco) OCT image
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $S _ {O C T} ^ {(m o c o)} (x, z) = A _ {m} ^ {j} (x, z) \exp \left[ i (\phi_ {m} ^ {j} (x, z) - \Delta \phi_ {b u l k} ^ {(m)}) \right]$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
an axial motion corrected (moco) image is generated:

$$
S _ {O C T} ^ {(m o c o)} (x, z) = A _ {m} ^ {j} (x, z) \exp \left[ i (\phi_ {m} ^ {j} (x, z) - \Delta \phi_ {b u l k} ^ {(m)}) \right]. \tag {40}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.symbol: $S _ {O C T} ^ {(j, m o c o)} (x, z)$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Complex signal aligned with respect to the reference frame in an amplitude weighted manner
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $S _ {O C T} ^ {(j, m o c o)} (x, z) = \sqrt {A _ {j} (x , z) A _ {r e f} (x , z)} \exp \left[ i \left(\phi_ {j} (x, z) - \phi_ {r e f} (x, z)\right) \right]$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
The phasors in all pixel locations $(x,z)$ of the subsequent frames are then aligned with respect to those in the reference frame by multiplying them to the conjugate complex of $S_{OCT}^{(ref)}(x,z)$ in an amplitude weighted manner,

$$
S _ {O C T} ^ {(j, m o c o)} (x, z) = \sqrt {A _ {j} (x , z) A _ {r e f} (x , z)} \exp \left[ i \left(\phi_ {j} (x, z) - \phi_ {r e f} (x, z)\right) \right]. \tag {41}
$$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: phase difference between the j-th frame and the reference frame
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \Delta\phi_{j}(x,z)=\phi_{j}(x,z)-\phi_{ref}(x,z) $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: averaged phase difference
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $\overline {{{{\Delta \phi_ {j}}}}} (x, z) = \arg \left[ \sum_ {x = x - \Delta x / 2} ^ {x + \Delta x / 2} \sum_ {z = z - \Delta z / 2} ^ {z + \Delta z / 2} A _ {j} (x, z) A _ {\text { ref }} (x, z) \exp [ i \Delta \phi_ {j} (x, z) ] \right]. \tag {42}$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \overline {{{{\Delta \phi_ {j}}}}} (x, z) = \arg \left[ \sum_ {x = x - \Delta x / 2} ^ {x + \Delta x / 2} \sum_ {z = z - \Delta z / 2} ^ {z + \Delta z / 2} A _ {j} (x, z) A _ {\text { ref }} (x, z) \exp [ i \Delta \phi_ {j} (x, z) ] \right]. \tag {42} $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Gaussian error function
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote: $$ \operatorname{erf}(u)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^{u}\exp\left[-v^{2}/2\right]dv $$

Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.symbol: $S _ {O C T} ^ {(j, \overline {{m o c o}})} (x, z)$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quantity: Motion-corrected OCT signal for the j-th frame
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.definition: $S _ {O C T} ^ {(j, \overline {{m o c o}})} (x, z) = \sqrt {A _ {j} (x , z) A _ {r e f} (x , z)} \exp \left[ i \left(\phi_ {j} (x, z) - \overline {{\Delta \phi_ {j}}} (x, z)\right) \right]$
Signal_averaging_OCT_BOE.quote:
If now, in a third step, the locally averaged phase difference map (Eq. (42)) is used to correct the phasors of the j-th frame with respect to the reference frame,

$$
S _ {O C T} ^ {(j, \overline {{m o c o}})} (x, z) = \sqrt {A _ {j} (x , z) A _ {r e f} (x , z)} \exp \left[ i \left(\phi_ {j} (x, z) - \overline {{\Delta \phi_ {j}}} (x, z)\right) \right], \tag {45}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $\overline {{\log \pi_ {\theta}}} (y \mid x) = \frac {1}{| y |} \log \pi_ {\theta} (y \mid x) = \frac {1}{| y |} \sum_ {t = 1} ^ {| y |} \log P _ {\theta} \left(y _ {t} \mid x, y _ {<   t}\right)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
reference-free methods commonly employ the length-normalized log-probability:

$$
\overline {{\log \pi_ {\theta}}} (y \mid x) = \frac {1}{| y |} \log \pi_ {\theta} (y \mid x) = \frac {1}{| y |} \sum_ {t = 1} ^ {| y |} \log P _ {\theta} \left(y _ {t} \mid x, y _ {<   t}\right), \tag {1}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $\overline{LP}(y) = -\overline{\log\pi_{\theta}}(y \mid x)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote: Conjecture 1 (Uncertainty Reduction with Sequence Length Assertion (URSLA)). Let $\overline{LP}(y) = -\overline{\log\pi_{\theta}}(y \mid x)$ be the average per-token negative log-probability (a measure of model uncertainty or perplexity) for a response $y$ .

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $L _ {\text {S i m P O}} (\theta) = - \mathbb {E} _ {(x, y _ {w}, y _ {l}) \sim \mathcal {D}} \left[ \log \sigma \left(\beta \overline {{\log \pi_ {\theta}}} (y _ {w} | x) - \beta \overline {{\log \pi_ {\theta}}} (y _ {l} | x) - \gamma\right) \right]$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
The objective maximizes the margin between the scores of the winning and losing responses:

$$
L _ {\text {S i m P O}} (\theta) = - \mathbb {E} _ {(x, y _ {w}, y _ {l}) \sim \mathcal {D}} \left[ \log \sigma \left(\beta \overline {{\log \pi_ {\theta}}} (y _ {w} | x) - \beta \overline {{\log \pi_ {\theta}}} (y _ {l} | x) - \gamma\right) \right], \tag {3}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quantity: model distribution derived from the policy-reference ratio
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $p_i^{\mathrm{model}} \propto \pi_\theta(y_i|x) / \pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_i|x)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote: It is a reference-based method that minimizes the cross-entropy between a reward-derived target distribution $(p_i^{\mathrm{target}} \propto e^{r_i})$ and a model distribution derived from the policy-reference ratio $(p_i^{\mathrm{model}} \propto \pi_\theta(y_i|x) / \pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_i|x))$ .

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.symbol: $L _ {\text {I n f o N C A}} (\theta ; \pi_ {\text {r e f}})$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $L _ {\text {I n f o N C A}} (\theta ; \pi_ {\text {r e f}}) = - \mathbb {E} _ {x \sim \mathcal {D}} \left[ \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {K} p _ {i} ^ {\text {t a r g e t}} \log p _ {i} ^ {\text {m o d e l}} \right]$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
Its loss is:

$$
L _ {\text {I n f o N C A}} (\theta ; \pi_ {\text {r e f}}) = - \mathbb {E} _ {x \sim \mathcal {D}} \left[ \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {K} p _ {i} ^ {\text {t a r g e t}} \log p _ {i} ^ {\text {m o d e l}} \right]. \tag {4}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $s_{\theta}(y|x) = \log (\pi_{\theta}(y|x) / \pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y|x))$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
Using a reference-based score $s_{\theta}(y|x) = \log (\pi_{\theta}(y|x) / \pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y|x))$ , its loss is:

$$
s_{\theta}(y|x) = \log (\pi_{\theta}(y|x) / \pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y|x))
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $L _ {\mathrm {M P O}} (\theta ; \pi_ {\mathrm {r e f}}) = - \mathbb {E} _ {x \sim \mathcal {D}} \left[ \log \frac {\sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+}} w _ {y} \exp \left(\beta s _ {\theta} (y \mid x)\right)}{\sum_ {y \in Y} w _ {y} \exp \left(\beta s _ {\theta} (y \mid x)\right)} \right]$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
its loss is:

$$
L _ {\mathrm {M P O}} (\theta ; \pi_ {\mathrm {r e f}}) = - \mathbb {E} _ {x \sim \mathcal {D}} \left[ \log \frac {\sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+}} w _ {y} \exp \left(\beta s _ {\theta} (y \mid x)\right)}{\sum_ {y \in Y} w _ {y} \exp \left(\beta s _ {\theta} (y \mid x)\right)} \right]. \tag {5}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $s(y) = \beta \cdot \overline{\log\pi_{\theta}}(y|x)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
Let the base score for a response be its scaled, length-normalized log-probability, $s(y) = \beta \cdot \overline{\log\pi_{\theta}}(y|x)$ , where $\beta$ is an inverse temperature.

$$
s(y) = \beta \cdot \overline{\log\pi_{\theta}}(y|x)
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.symbol: $L _ {\text {R E F A - D y n a m i c}} (\theta)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $L _ {\text {R E F A - D y n a m i c}} (\theta) = - \log \frac {\sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+}} e ^ {s (y)}}{\sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+}} e ^ {s (y)} + \gamma \sum_ {y \in Y ^ {-}} e ^ {s (y)}}$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
The REFA-Dynamic loss is:

$$
L _ {\text {R E F A - D y n a m i c}} (\theta) = - \log \frac {\sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+}} e ^ {s (y)}}{\sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+}} e ^ {s (y)} + \gamma \sum_ {y \in Y ^ {-}} e ^ {s (y)}}. \tag {6}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $s_{\mathrm{wtd}}(y) = s(y) + \alpha (r_y - \bar{r})$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote: $s_{\mathrm{wtd}}(y) = s(y) + \alpha (r_y - \bar{r})$ , where $\alpha$ is a hyperparameter.

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: hyperparameter
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote: $s_{\mathrm{wtd}}(y) = s(y) + \alpha (r_y - \bar{r})$ , where $\alpha$ is a hyperparameter.

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $\mathcal {R} _ {\text {t a r g e t}} (\theta) = \sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+} \cup Y ^ {-}} \lambda P _ {\theta} (\operatorname {E O S} \text {a t} | y |) \cdot \max  (0, \text {T A R G E T L E N G T H} - | y |)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
The regularizer is formulated as:

$$
\mathcal {R} _ {\text {t a r g e t}} (\theta) = \sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+} \cup Y ^ {-}} \lambda P _ {\theta} (\operatorname {E O S} \text {a t} | y |) \cdot \max  (0, \text {T A R G E T L E N G T H} - | y |), \tag {7}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $L _ {\mathrm {R E F A}} (\theta) = - \log \frac {\sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+}} e ^ {s (y)}}{\sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+}} e ^ {s (y)} + \gamma \sum_ {y \in Y ^ {-}} e ^ {s (y)}} + \mathcal {R} _ {\text {t a r g e t}} (\theta)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
The Final REFA Loss. By integrating this regularizer with the REFA-Dynamic objective from Eq. 6, we arrive at the final loss function for our primary method:

$$
L _ {\mathrm {R E F A}} (\theta) = - \log \frac {\sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+}} e ^ {s (y)}}{\sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+}} e ^ {s (y)} + \gamma \sum_ {y \in Y ^ {-}} e ^ {s (y)}} + \mathcal {R} _ {\text {t a r g e t}} (\theta). \tag {8}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition:
$\mathcal {R} _ {\text {i n d e p}} (\theta) = - \sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+} \cup Y ^ {-}} \lambda \log
P _ {\theta} (\operatorname {E O S} \text {a t p o s i t i o n} | y |)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
It is formulated as a penalty on the negative log-probability of the EOS token:

$$
\mathcal {R} _ {\text {i n d e p}} (\theta) = - \sum_ {y \in Y ^ {+} \cup Y ^ {-}} \lambda \log
P _ {\theta} (\operatorname {E O S} \text {a t p o s i t i o n} | y |). \tag {9}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.symbol: $\mathcal {R} _ {\text {b u d g e t e d}} (\theta)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $\mathcal {R} _ {\text {b u d g e t e d}} (\theta) = \lambda \left(\frac {1}{b} \sum_ {t = 1} ^ {b - 1} P _ {\theta} (\text {E O S a t t o k e n} t) - \frac {1}{| y | - b} \sum_ {t = b + 1} ^ {| y |} P _ {\theta} (\text {E O S a t t o k e n} t)\right)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
The formulation creates a "push-pull" dynamic around the budget:

$$
\mathcal {R} _ {\text {b u d g e t e d}} (\theta) = \lambda \left(\frac {1}{b} \sum_ {t = 1} ^ {b - 1} P _ {\theta} (\text {E O S a t t o k e n} t) - \frac {1}{| y | - b} \sum_ {t = b + 1} ^ {| y |} P _ {\theta} (\text {E O S a t t o k e n} t)\right). \tag {10}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quantity: log-ratio of policy to reference distribution
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $r _ {\theta} (x, y _ {i}) := \log \frac {\pi_ {\theta} \left(y _ {i} \mid x\right)}{\mu \left(y _ {i} \mid x\right)}$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
We define the ratio:

$$
r _ {\theta} (x, y _ {i}) := \log \frac {\pi_ {\theta} \left(y _ {i} \mid x\right)}{\mu \left(y _ {i} \mid x\right)}. \tag {11}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $p _ {i} ^ {\text {t a r g e t}} := \frac {e ^ {\alpha r _ {i}}}{\sum_ {j = 1} ^ {K} e ^ {\alpha r _ {j}}}$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
The target distribution derived from the rewards is given by a softmax transformation:

$$
p _ {i} ^ {\text {t a r g e t}} := \frac {e ^ {\alpha r _ {i}}}{\sum_ {j = 1} ^ {K} e ^ {\alpha r _ {j}}}, \tag {12}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $p _ {i} ^ {\text {m o d e l}} := \frac {e ^ {r _ {\theta} (x , y _ {i})}}{\sum_ {j = 1} ^ {K} e ^ {r _ {\theta} (x , y _ {j})}}$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
we define the model distribution as:

$$
p _ {i} ^ {\text {m o d e l}} := \frac {e ^ {r _ {\theta} (x , y _ {i})}}{\sum_ {j = 1} ^ {K} e ^ {r _ {\theta} (x , y _ {j})}}. \tag {13}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.symbol: $L _ {\text {I n f o N C A}} (\theta)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: The cross-entropy between the target distribution $p_i^{\mathrm{target}}$ and the model distribution $p_i^{\mathrm{model}}$.
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
The InfoNCA loss is the cross-entropy between the target distribution $p_i^{\mathrm{target}}$ and the model distribution $p_i^{\mathrm{model}}$ :

$$
L _ {\text {I n f o N C A}} (\theta) = - \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {K} p _ {i} ^ {\text {t a r g e t}} \log p _ {i} ^ {\text {m o d e l}}. \tag {14}
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $\delta_{ik} = 1$ if $i = k$ and 0 otherwise.
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
$$
\frac {\partial \log p _ {k} ^ {\mathrm {m o d e l}}}{\partial r _ {\theta} (x , y _ {i})} = \delta_ {i k} - p _ {i} ^ {\mathrm {m o d e l}},
$$

where $\delta_{ik} = 1$ if $i = k$ and 0 otherwise.

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quantity: Sum of the ratio of policy probability to reference probability over all candidates
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $A := \sum_{j = 1} ^ {K} \frac {\pi_ {\theta} (y _ {j} | x)}{\mu (y _ {j} | x)}$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
Define:

$$
A := \sum_ {j = 1} ^ {K} \frac {\pi_ {\theta} (y _ {j} | x)}{\mu (y _ {j} | x)}.
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $\hat {\pi} _ {\theta} (y _ {i} | x) = \frac {\pi_ {\theta} (y _ {i} | x)}{\sum_ {k = 1} ^ {K} \pi_ {\theta} (y _ {k} | x)} = \frac {p _ {i} ^ {\mathrm {t a r g e t}} \mu (y _ {i} | x)}{\sum_ {k = 1} ^ {K} p _ {k} ^ {\mathrm {t a r g e t}} \mu (y _ {k} | x)}$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
If we subsequently impose normalization to interpret $\pi_{\theta}(y_i|x)$ as a probability distribution, we would set:

$$
\hat {\pi} _ {\theta} (y _ {i} | x) = \frac {\pi_ {\theta} (y _ {i} | x)}{\sum_ {k = 1} ^ {K} \pi_ {\theta} (y _ {k} | x)} = \frac {p _ {i} ^ {\mathrm {t a r g e t}} \mu (y _ {i} | x)}{\sum_ {k = 1} ^ {K} p _ {k} ^ {\mathrm {t a r g e t}} \mu (y _ {k} | x)}.
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quantity: Normalization constant for the target-weighted reference model probabilities
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $M := \sum_ {k = 1} ^ {K} p _ {k} ^ {\text {t a r g e t}} \mu \left(y _ {k} | x\right)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
Define:

$$
M := \sum_ {k = 1} ^ {K} p _ {k} ^ {\text {t a r g e t}} \mu \left(y _ {k} | x\right),
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $r_{\theta}(x,y) \coloneqq \log \pi_{\theta}(y|x)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote: If we were to remove $\mu(y|x)$ from the formulation, i.e., consider a scenario where $r_{\theta}(x,y) \coloneqq \log \pi_{\theta}(y|x)$ without dividing by $\mu(y|x)$ , then the model distribution $p_i^{\mathrm{model}}$ would directly be:

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $\ell_ {i} (\theta) := - p _ {i} ^ {\text {t a r g e t}} \log p _ {i} ^ {\text {m o d e l}}$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
Lemma 1 (Gradient of a Single-Term Objective). Let $\ell_i(\theta)$ be defined as:

$$
\ell_ {i} (\theta) := - p _ {i} ^ {\text {t a r g e t}} \log p _ {i} ^ {\text {m o d e l}},
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quantity: Partial derivative of the single-term objective with respect to the model probability of the target item
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $\frac {\partial \ell_ {i} (\theta)}{\partial \pi_ {\theta} (y _ {i} | x)} = - p _ {i} ^ {\mathrm {t a r g e t}} \left(\frac {1}{\pi_ {\theta} (y _ {i} | x)} - \frac {1}{\sum_ {j = 1} ^ {K} \pi_ {\theta} (y _ {j} | x)}\right)$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
Then, the partial derivatives of $\ell_i(\theta)$ with respect to $\pi_{\theta}(y_i|x)$ and $\pi_{\theta}(y_j|x)$ for $j \neq i$ are:

$$
\frac {\partial \ell_ {i} (\theta)}{\partial \pi_ {\theta} (y _ {i} | x)} = - p _ {i} ^ {\mathrm {t a r g e t}} \left(\frac {1}{\pi_ {\theta} (y _ {i} | x)} - \frac {1}{\sum_ {j = 1} ^ {K} \pi_ {\theta} (y _ {j} | x)}\right),
$$

SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quantity: Partial derivative of the single-term objective with respect to the model probability of a non-target item
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.definition: $\frac {\partial \ell_ {i} (\theta)}{\partial \pi_ {\theta} (y _ {j} | x)} = p _ {i} ^ {\text {t a r g e t}} \frac {1}{\sum_ {k = 1} ^ {K} \pi_ {\theta} (y _ {k} | x)}$
SimPO_Simple_Preference_Optimization_wit.quote:
and for each $j\neq i$

To incorporate a preference on the EOS probability, we define a regularization term $\mathcal{R}(\theta)$ that depends on $P_{\theta}(\mathrm{EOS}|$ tokens before EOS in $y$ ).

$$

the total expected reward across the dataset is

$$

$$

Then, the sampling is performed according to the probability:

$$

$$

We define the $\gamma$ -reweighted distribution $\widehat{\mathrm{P}}(w|c) \propto \mathrm{P}(w) \cdot \mathrm{P}(c|w)^{\gamma}$ , and approximate it with CFG as $\widehat{\mathrm{P}}(w|c) \propto \frac{\mathrm{P}(w|c)^{\gamma}}{\mathrm{P}(w)^{\gamma-1}}$

For the non-compact support integrals, it is sufficient to consider the following integral:

$$

$$

$$

$$
